subject.title: [Feature]: Session grouping, unread state, and full session controls on web, iOS, and Android

question: Should OpenClaw accept this cross-client session-manager direction now, and should unread state plus transcript forking be owned by the gateway protocol exactly along the proposed shape?
rationale: The issue spans additive protocol fields, persisted session semantics, web and mobile UI parity, and a protected maintainer label, so automation should not choose the product/API contract alone.

options.title: Stage Gateway Contract First
options.body: Approve the direction but split implementation into gateway unread/fork semantics first, then separate web, iOS, and Android client PRs with proof.

options.title: Narrow To Existing Web Controls
options.body: Limit near-term work to web sidebar/Sessions page parity using existing category, pin, archive, label, and delete primitives while deferring unread and mobile work.

options.title: Defer Mobile Session Manager
options.body: Keep this as a design issue until maintainers decide the mobile session-management UX and whether gateway unread state belongs in the public protocol.

recommendation.title: Stage Gateway Contract First
recommendation.body: Approve the direction but split implementation into gateway unread/fork semantics first, then separate web, iOS, and Android client PRs with proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the recent web session grouping/sidebar and gateway session-management work that the proposed design builds on.
